lines.en: Michael, you remember my daughter, Melissa?
Oh, yes. Hello. How are you?
Good to see you. Wow, you've really grown up.
You know what? Don't mind me saying so.
She has turned into a stone-cold fox.
Better keep the frat boys away from her.
I'm in eighth grade.
-Oh. -She's in middle school.
Yeah, middle school's amazing.
It is extraordinary. An extraordinary time.
I drink, like, a hundred iced macchiatos a day
and practically nothing else.
Wow.
There's a really cool coffee place, Jitters,
at the Steamtown Mall.
You ever been there?
No.
You've never been to Jitters?
Ryan, you are so dorky.
Give me your number so I can text you.
Um...
Come on.
Can I have an email address?
...but I just thought you should know.
I think something a little fishy is going on.
A little fishy?
Yeah. I mean, I've been noticing them all day.
I think I have a good one.
That little girl is a child.
I don't want to see you sniffing around her anymore this afternoon.
Do you understand?
Boy, have you lost your mind 'cause I'll help you find it.
What you're looking for? Ain't nobody gonna help you out there.
Jesus can come through that door and he's not gonna help you
if you don't stop sniffing after my child.
Okay.
Stanley yelled at me today.
That was one of the most frightening experiences of my life.
"Hi, Ryan."
"Hi, Ryan."
"Hey."
"How are you doing? I've... I've missed you."
"I've missed you, too."
"Don't you remember me?"
"Um, yeah, you gotta give me a hint."
"Um, did you meet me at the gym?"
"No. Who the hell is Ryan talking to?"
"Are you a client of her, Riffler?"
"Oh, not again."
"Melissa!"
"Daddy!"
"Wait for me outside."
"God."
"She is 16 years old. What is wrong with you?"
"No, no, no, no."
"You came right up to me."
"No, no, no, no, no, no, no, you playing this whole thing, slinking and slinking around a bar like some low-woking louser."
"No, no, no, no, don't apologize now. You ought to stay away from my daughter. You want to end up on the Stone Phillips nasty man smoke. Don't try to ride."
"You want to sit in the ass. You don't think you've been a dog before you think you're gonna run for me, huh? I'll be on your tail like a hot wind."
